chunks: Visit the House on the Day of Sacrifice or on the following day while you are in a state of ghusl (ritual bath), and do not delay visiting it beyond your day or the next day, for it is not for the Mutamatti‘ to delay it, while latitude is given to the Mufrid to delay it.
And say on your way, while heading toward the visitation, whatever you are able of glorifying Allah, praising Him, and sending blessings upon the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم and his family.

Then when you reach the door of the mosque, stand there and say: “O Allah, help me in my rites, keep them sound for me, and keep me safe through them. I ask You with the plea of the sick, the humble, the one confessing his sin, that You forgive my sins and return me with my need fulfilled. O Allah, I am Your servant, the land is Your land, and the House is Your House. I have come seeking Your mercy and pursuing Your good pleasure, following Your command, content with Your decree. I ask You with the plea of the one driven to You, obedient to Your command, apprehensive of Your punishment, fearful of Your chastisement. I ask You to grant me Your pardon and protect me, by Your mercy, from the Fire.”

key_terms.نُسُكِي: my rites of worship, especially hajj rituals
key_terms.يَوْمَ ٱلنَّحْرِ: the Day of Sacrifice during hajj rites
key_terms.ٱلْبَيْتَ: the Sacred House, meaning the Ka'bah

ai.seo_question: What should be said and done when visiting the Ka'bah on the Day of Sacrifice or the following day?
ai.summary: This passage gives guidance for visiting the Ka'bah after the rites of Mina, specifying the timing for the visit and distinguishing between the Mutamatti‘ and the Mufrid pilgrim. It also teaches remembrance of Allah and a supplication to be recited at the mosque entrance, expressing humility, obedience, hope for mercy, and seeking protection from the Fire.
